summary.value:
This paper studies in-context watermarking for LLMs by embedding watermarks into LLM-generated text via prompt engineering.

Strengths:
(1) model-agnostic approach.
(2) overall comprehensive evaluation, with the trade-offs among several aspects including LLM requirements, detectability, robustness, and text quality. 
(2) overall clear writing.

Weaknesses: 
(1) lack of evaluation of the true positive rate at a very low false positive rate.
(2) lack of human evaluation.
(3) lack of evaluation of detectability of ICWs after a multi-turn conversation.
(4) improper position of the novelty of the proposed work in the context of the existing work (by one reviewer).
(5) practical limitation of the proposed work that limits the applicability of the proposed method (by one reviewer).

reviewer_concerns.value:
(1) lack of evaluation of the true positive rate at a very low false positive rate was addressed.
(2) the concern regarding evaluating with one more LLM was addressed.
(3) the concern regarding the multi-turn conversation was also addressed.
(4) Lack of human evaluation is still outstanding.
